census.reason: The label data-oriented design does not choose a layout. Access patterns, overflow semantics and conversion/identity costs determine whether splitting fields helps; removing overflow checks to obtain SIMD changes the correctness contract.

Small-buffer optimization introduces two ownership regimes and an often-hidden object-type problem. An address satisfying alignment is not proof that a declared unsigned-char array may be accessed through any desired struct pointer.

Ordinary word addition is not lane-wise addition; carries and saturation require a proof. A benchmark over only identical lanes can miss a carry leaking into a different neighboring lane.

Dense iteration and stable addresses can coexist only by choosing what moves. Many sparse-set bugs repair one mapping but forget the inverse; generation counters eventually wrap unless exhaustion is part of the contract.

An archetype label does not teach migration atomicity or query invalidation. Deleting the old row before discovering a full destination loses an entity even though the numerical component code is correct.

Cheap root copying shifts costs into path cloning and retained history. Const qualification does not freeze aliases, and a path-copy algorithm that silently mutates one old node breaks every older version sharing it.

Owner-bound slot generations admit a stable logical identity while dense IDs move. The criteria require reuse rejection, finite-generation retirement, inverse-map repair and the counterexample that a generation check does not revoke a retained raw pointer.
census.scope: C handle admission and bounded reuse histories, with X-T03-005 as an explicit prerequisite. This is not a static lifetime proof or a concurrent reclamation guarantee.
